'''Holothrillers''' were a [[Holoshow/Legends|holoshow]] genre that usually invoked a sense of thrills and featured a lot of action. A frequent theme of the genre is that, unless the villain's body is explicitly seen in the end, they aren't assumed to be dead by the audience even if the villain in-universe is believed to be dead.

During a briefing in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] relating to discoveries that might link to the [[Rakatan revolt]], [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] mockingly stated to Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]], a researcher for [[pre-Republic era]] studies at the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology]] giving the briefing, that he re-evaluated his expertise to be for holothrillers as well as for [[science fiction]]. Bowen would later use Motti's earlier reference to the work, specifically the aspect of a villain's body not being present to mean survival, to infer that the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] may have had a chance of surviving.

By [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], holothrillers were also made relating to [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. Han purchased copies of the films made after him such as ''[[Han Solo and the Pirates of Kessel]]'' and ''[[Han Solo in the Lair of the Space Slugs|Han Solo and the Lair of the Space Slugs]]'' to watch on [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|his ship]] while he waited for [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] to finish her diplomatic missions. Skywalker, however, cited many historical inaccuracies in two of the films: ''[[Luke Skywalker and the Dragons of Tatooine]]'' and ''[[Luke Skywalker and the Jedi's Revenge]]'', the latter of which he took particular exception to due to its depiction of him killing [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to avenge [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], expressing disgust at it.

{{Stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Holothrillers were first mentioned in the 2008 novel ''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]'' by [[Matthew Stover]]. In a blog post, Stover implied that the events of ''Shadows of Mindor'' itself had been an in-universe holothriller.
